description:
Initialization: Build routes by greedily inserting orders in ascending delivery-window deadline order, then initialize the current and best solutions.

Search:
- Operator selection: Select a destroy operator and a repair operator independently by weighted roulette, related to ALG-003; the scoring rules differ from that reference.
- Destroy: Remove orders using random, relatedness, worst-contribution, or whole-route removal. The relatedness variant uses one seed and picks the closest orders; the worst-contribution variant ranks once. They differ from the randomized, iterative paper-based references ALG-008 and ALG-009.
- Repair: Reinsert removed orders with greedy, regret-2, or noise-perturbed insertion; regret-2 is related to ALG-004 but uses the case implementation. Discard an attempt if repair fails or the implementation's solution-feasibility check fails.
- Acceptance and scoring: Apply simulated annealing to the candidate, related to ALG-007; this case has a minimum temperature. Score the selected operators for a new best, an improvement, or an accepted candidate; update their weights and cool the temperature at segment boundaries.
- Route refinement: At the configured interval after a successful attempt, use CP-SAT to reorder individual routes. Per-route candidates are checked by the implementation; changed routes replace the current routes when the reported cost is finite.
- Termination: Stop at the iteration limit or when the wall-clock limit is noticed at the start of an iteration.

Scope: This is a third-party ALNS + CP-SAT variant for PDPTW, not the 2006 authors' implementation. It does not call the project reference implementations. Its initial insertion and feasibility/cost checks have known limitations documented in the accompanying case note; validate returned solutions independently.
